title: Dark Chocolate Orange Mousse
summary: Airy dark chocolate mousse flavoured with fresh orange juice and zest, topped with a candied orange slice.

ingredients.item: dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
ingredients.note: check the label for soya and milk
Use pasteurised eggs (see the egg safety tip).

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
small orange, cut into 6 thin slices

steps.title: Orange slices
steps.text: dissolve the 50 g sugar in the water in the frying pan, add the slices and simmer very gently 25-30 min until the peel is translucent; cool on baking paper. Slow simmering softens the peel so it is tender, not bitter.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: in the heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, melt the chocolate with the cocoa, espresso, hot orange juice and zest, stirring until glossy. Remove from the heat. Hot juice in place of water carries the orange through the chocolate.

steps.title: Yolks
steps.text: beat the yolks, salt and 1 tbsp of the sugar briefly, then beat in the melted chocolate. Cool 5 min to just warm. Yolks add richness and help the mousse set.

steps.title: Whites
steps.text: whip the whites until foamy, add the remaining sugar and whip to soft peaks. Loosen the chocolate with a quarter of them, then fold in the rest gently. The whites hold the air that makes the mousse light.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: whip the cream to soft peaks and fold through until no white streaks remain. Soft peaks fold in smoothly.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: divide between the bowls, cover and chill 3 h or more. Top each with a candied orange slice and a few strands of zest. The mousse firms as the chocolate cools.

tips: Egg safety: Use pasteurised eggs. If you can't get them, use the 71 °C cooked-egg method (given in the tips), or skip this recipe if you are pregnant, very young, older or have a weak immune system.

71 °C cooked-egg method: whisk the yolks with 15 g of the sugar and 2 tbsp water in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until the mixture reaches 71 °C and thickens, about 4 min, then whisk it into the chocolate. Whisk the whites with the other 15 g sugar in a clean heatproof bowl over the same pan until they reach 71 °C, take off the heat and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks (a Swiss meringue), then fold in as described.
A common mistake is overmixing after the whites go in; stop folding when no white streaks remain.
Grate only the orange part of the peel; the white pith is bitter.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Store the candied slices separately in an airtight box for up to 1 week.
